messages:
jin: Heads-up — I ran a co-residency experiment with two medium LMs + small reranker on one A100, trying buffer reuse across models. Results are noisy, seeing OOMs during long-context churn. :thinking:
arya: Can you paste the exact config you used? especially allocator profile and batch sizes.
sam: Also which kernels were picked? fallback kernels can blow up workspace.
jin: Config: soft_segment=on, workspace_target_mb=1024, kv_prefetch=enabled, batch_autotune=off. Kernel selection was default (auto) — saw a fallback to cuBLAS_fp32 on step 120.
mike: OOMs when chunking long prompts + attention cache repopulation is classic. Did you enable incremental KV reuse?
jin: We had kv_reuse_mode=shadow (keeps references but rematerializes on demand). That seemed to thrash memory.
tess: Try kv_reuse_mode=aggressive-compact (compress hot prefixes) + workspace_target_mb=800. Also reduce max_batch_tokens to 512 for the medium models.
arya: Also check kernel selection logs: new selector will pick matmul_algo=algo3 for 2048 seqs; fallback to algo1 if workspace not available. That fallback increases temporary buffer by ~600MB.
sam: Can you share the perf log snippet? even a small dump helps.
jin: Pasting snippet:
```
[1937654321] model:medium-A selected kernel: algo3 (workspace 1.2GB)
[1937654360] kernel fallback -> algo1 (workspace 1.8GB)
[1937654361] allocator: attempted soft-split, failed to reclaim 700MB -> OOM on alloc(933MB)
```
mike: That fallback is the root. Kernel selector should consider soft-segment reservations and current kv cache footprint before choosing algo3.
tess: We can add a pre-check hook in selector: query allocator.free_reserve_mb() and kv.current_active_mb(). If free < required + reserve_threshold, pick smaller workspace kernel.
arya: Agree. Also batch_autotune off means we didn't adapt batch sizes after noticing spill. Maybe enable batch_autotune with conservative headroom.
sam: Another mitigation: preemptively evict cold KV slices for the background reranker while serving the main model. Evicting 200–300MB can avoid fallback.
jin: Good call. I ran a quick manual evict on reranker and the run completed once. We should automate as policy: model-priority tags + preemptive-evict rules.
infra-bot: CI run 193765-evict-policy-test started on pool-gpu-a100-3 (job id 5843).
arya: We should also examine buffer reuse pattern. Right now buffers are per-model and not reused across models even when identical shapes. A cross-model free list keyed by (dtype,shape,alignment) could reduce transient allocs.
mike: Cross-model reuse plus a soft partitioning layer (soft quotas per model with reclaim callbacks) would give isolation while allowing reuse.
tess: For profiling: capture per-kernel workspace and per-model kv footprint in a single timeline. Use trace flags: --trace-ws --trace-kv-sizes. Then run a mixed workload over 15 minutes.
sam: I suspect the perf regression in prior run came from enabling compact-kv + aggressive kernel, which increased CPU GC time and stalled allocator callbacks. Need to measure callback latency.
jin: Action items: (1) add selector pre-check for free_reserve & kv footprint; (2) prototype cross-model buffer free list; (3) enable batch_autotune conservative; (4) add preemptive-evict policy rules and test in CI. I'll spin up an experiment branch.
arya: +1. If you want, I can take (2) — I sketched a design for shape-keyed freelist.
jin: Please do, that'd help. I'll own selector pre-check and evict policy.
mike: I'll coordinate kernel fallback metrics and add a dashboard tile for fallback frequency vs oom events.
infra-bot: CI run 193765-evict-policy-test finished: FAILED (oom reproducer hit at step 45). Logs uploaded to /artifacts/5843/oom-fail.log
jin: Thanks infra-bot — I'll attach logs to the PR. Meeting sync tomorrow 10am to go over experiment results?
tess: Works for me. :thumbsup:
